background: Lloyds Bank plc is the main ring-fenced bank of Lloyds Banking Group, the UK's largest retail bank, funded by UK personal and business deposits and lending mainly on residential mortgages, cards, motor finance and to UK companies.
synthesis: Lloyds Bank is rated AA- on average across all three main agencies, the weakest of them at A+, all three on a stable outlook, after a one-notch upgrade by one of the three on 12 May 2026. Capital is mixed against UK majors, leverage of 5.1% in the top quarter but CET1 of 13.6% just below the peer median, and liquidity is the weak spot, LCR of 134% and NSFR of 118% both in the bottom quarter. Since 30 Jun 2025 leverage has fallen 0.3 points while CET1, LCR and NSFR have been broadly flat (figures to 30 Jun 2026). The newest flagged item, on 2 Oct 2026, is an online banking outage, with £1.2bn of fraud claims over the Arena Television loans before it.
